method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Redback bites can cause severe pain — adequate analgesia is the priority. Significant envenoming is rare.**
claims.source_text: Redback bites can cause severe pain and adequate analgesia is a priority … Redback spiders rarely cause significant envenoming
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cupboard/brown house spiders (*Steatoda*) cause similar symptoms and are treated the same way.** White-tailed spiders may cause only local irritation or inflammation.
claims.source_text: Cupboard/ brown house spiders (Steatoda species) also cause similar symptoms and are treated in the same manner as red backs. … Other spiders, including white tailed spiders (Lampona sp), may cause minor symptoms such as local irritation/ inflammation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Necrotising arachnidism** — small ulcers to spreading necrosis — **has been shown to be unrelated to spider bites.**
claims.source_text: Necrotising arachnidism is a skin syndrome of unknown aetiology with small ulcers to spreading necrosis. It has been shown to be unrelated to spider bites
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess children whose pain is not controlled by simple analgesia.** Diagnosis rests on a typical history; severity on the pain and any systemic features.
claims.source_text: Children requiring assessment Patients with pain which is not controlled by simple analgesia … Diagnosis is made on the basis of a typical history. A spider may be seen. … Severity is determined by the clinical picture of the severity of pain and any associated systemic features.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The bite isn't immediately painful; pain builds over minutes to hours**, radiates to regional nodes, proximal limb, abdomen, chest or back, and may last days. ⚠️ **In an infant it may present as intractable crying.**
claims.source_text: The bite is not immediately painful however pain at the bite site develops increasing over minutes to hours Radiating from the bite site to regional lymph nodes, proximal limb, abdomen, chest or back May last for days May present as intractable crying in an infant
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Systemic features:** headache, lethargy, malaise, nausea and vomiting, myalgia and neck spasm; sweating in unusual local or regional distributions; hypertension, irritability and agitation (possibly more common in children); priapism; rarely rhabdomyolysis or myocarditis.
claims.source_text: Generalised symptoms Headache Lethargy, malaise Nausea and vomiting Myalgia and neck spasm may occur … Sweating – local or regional in unusual distributions Autonomic features may include hypertension, irritability, and agitation; they are possibly seen more commonly in children than adults Priapism may occur Rarely rhabdomyolysis, myocarditis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Investigations are usually unnecessary**; check CK or ECG if rhabdomyolysis or myocarditis is suspected.
claims.source_text: Nil usually required. CK or ECG may be required if features suggestive of rhabdomyolysis or myocarditis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **First aid is an ice pack. Pressure immobilisation is NOT used.**
claims.source_text: First aid: Ice pack Pressure immobilisation is NOT used
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Analgesia:** paracetamol 15 mg/kg (max 1 g) and ibuprofen 10 mg/kg (max 400 mg), ± oxycodone 0.1 mg/kg (max 5 mg), ± fentanyl.
claims.source_text: Paracetamol 15 mg/kg (1 g) and ibuprofen 10 mg/kg (400 mg) +/- oxycodone 0.1 mg/kg (5 mg), +/- fentanyl
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss antivenom with a toxicologist only if analgesia fails.** Its aim is pain relief and the evidence for it is not strong, so give adequate analgesia first and discuss risks and benefits with the family.
claims.source_text: Discuss with a toxicologist (Victoria Poisons Information Centre - 13 11 26) if there is inadequate response to analgesia. … The primary aim of antivenom is to provide pain relief, so adequate analgesia should be provided first, particularly as there is not strong evidence to support the effect of antivenom. The risks / benefits should be discussed with the patient / family prior to administration.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Acute hypersensitivity risk is under 5%; no premedication is needed.** After treating a reaction, the antivenom can be restarted slowly. **Serum sickness can follow at 5–14 days.**
claims.source_text: There is a risk of acute hypersensitivity reaction of <5% (3.6% - 5.2) (see anaphylaxis). Premedication is not required. Once treated, the antivenom can be recommenced slowly. There is risk of serum sickness at 5-14 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dose: 2 ampoules (500 units each) CSL redback spider antivenom, diluted in 10 mL/kg up to 100 mL, IV over 20–30 minutes.** If IV access is difficult, give it undiluted IM.
claims.source_text: Dose: 2 ampoules (500 units each) CSL Redback Spider Antivenom, diluted in 10 ml/kg up to 100 ml, IV over 20 - 30 minutes … If IV access is difficult, undiluted antivenom can be given IM.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No effect in 2 hours: reconsider the diagnosis** and discuss with a clinical toxicologist.
claims.source_text: If no effect in 2 hours, reconsider diagnosis and discuss with a clinical toxicologist via the Poisons Information Centre.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Admission is not usually required.** Call the Poisons Information Centre if considering antivenom or if presentation is delayed.
claims.source_text: Consult Victorian Poisons Information Centre 13 11 26 for advice if considering antivenom, or in cases of delayed presentation. Admission is not usually required.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge once pain is controlled; after antivenom, observe at least 1 hour for recurrence** and give serum sickness information.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Adequate pain control Patients should be observed for at least 1 hour after antivenom for recurrence of symptoms. … Provision of information regarding serum sickness.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite – Redback Spider' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_%E2%80%93_Redback_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23
